name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q01 - Four-statement evaluation on physical properties of 3d metals

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the physical properties of transition elements:

I. With the exceptions of \(\mathrm{Zn}\), \(\mathrm{Cd}\), \(\mathrm{Hg}\), and \(\mathrm{Mn}\), transition metals have one or more typical metallic structures at normal temperatures.

II. Transition metals generally have high melting points due to the involvement of both \(ns\) and \((n-1)d\) electrons in interatomic metallic bonding.

III. Zinc has the highest enthalpy of atomisation in the \(3d\) transition series.

IV. From titanium (\(Z = 22\)) to copper (\(Z = 29\)), there is a significant general increase in density due to decreasing metallic radius and increasing atomic mass.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Physical properties of transition metals such as crystal structure, melting point, enthalpy of atomisation, and density are governed by metallic bonding involving \((n-1)d\) and \(ns\) electrons and trends in atomic mass and radius.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Claim
The claim regarding metallic structures is correct: nearly all transition metals adopt hcp, bcc, or ccp lattices at normal temperatures, except \(\mathrm{Zn}\), \(\mathrm{Cd}\), \(\mathrm{Hg}\), and \(\mathrm{Mn}\). The claim regarding melting points is also correct: participation of both \(ns\) and unpaired \((n-1)d\) electrons strengthens interatomic bonding and raises melting points. The claim regarding zinc's enthalpy of atomisation is incorrect: zinc has the lowest enthalpy of atomisation (\(126\,\mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}\)) in the \(3d\) series because no \(3d\) electrons participate in metallic bonding. The claim regarding density is correct: decreasing metallic radius combined with increasing atomic mass causes density to rise from \(\mathrm{Ti}\) to \(\mathrm{Cu}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning metallic structures, melting points, and density trend are correct, while the claim about zinc's enthalpy of atomisation is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q02 - Four-statement evaluation on halides, oxides, redox, and magnetism

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding \(3d\) transition metal compounds and ions:

I. In aqueous solution, \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) oxidises \(\mathrm{I^-}\) to \(\mathrm{I_2}\) and precipitates as \(\mathrm{CuI_2}\).

II. Oxygen stabilises higher oxidation states of transition metals better than fluorine because oxygen can form multiple bonds to metals.

III. In aqueous medium, \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) is a stronger reducing agent than \(\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}\).

IV. The permanganate ion (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\)) is diamagnetic, whereas the manganate ion (\(\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}\)) is paramagnetic due to one unpaired electron.

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Higher oxidation state stability, redox behaviour in aqueous solution, and magnetic properties of transition metal ions depend on electronic configurations, hydration enthalpies, and metal–ligand bonding.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Claim
The claim regarding the reaction of \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) with \(\mathrm{I^-}\) is incorrect: \(\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}\) oxidises \(\mathrm{I^-}\) to \(\mathrm{I_2}\), but the copper product precipitated is copper(I) iodide (\(\mathrm{Cu_2I_2}\)), not \(\mathrm{CuI_2}\). The claim regarding oxygen versus fluorine is correct: oxygen's ability to form multiple bonds allows it to stabilise higher oxidation states (such as \(+7\) in \(\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}\)) better than fluorine (highest manganese fluoride is \(\mathrm{MnF_4}\)). The claim regarding reducing strength is incorrect: \(\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}\) (\(d^4 \rightarrow d^3\), half-filled \(t_{2g}\)) is a stronger reducing agent in water than \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) (\(d^6 \rightarrow d^5\)). The claim regarding magnetism of \(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\) and \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}\) is correct: \(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\) has \(3d^0\) \(\mathrm{Mn(VII)}\) (diamagnetic), while \(\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}\) has \(3d^1\) \(\mathrm{Mn(VI)}\) (one unpaired electron, paramagnetic).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the claims regarding oxygen's stabilisation of higher oxidation states and the magnetic properties of permanganate and manganate ions are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_UNIT8_Q03 - Four-statement evaluation on oxoanions, titrations, lanthanoids, and actinoids

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding transition metal oxoanions and inner transition elements:

I. Chromate (\(\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}\)) and dichromate (\(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\)) ions are interconvertible in aqueous solution depending on \(\mathrm{pH}\), and chromium is in the \(+6\) oxidation state in both.

II. Permanganate titrations are best carried out in the presence of hydrochloric acid to maintain an acidic medium.

III. Lanthanoid contraction causes zirconium (\(\mathrm{Zr}\), \(160\,\mathrm{pm}\)) and hafnium (\(\mathrm{Hf}\), \(159\,\mathrm{pm}\)) to have almost identical atomic radii.

IV. In the first half of the actinoid series, the maximum oxidation state increases from \(+4\) in \(\mathrm{Th}\) to \(+5\) in \(\mathrm{Pa}\), \(+6\) in \(\mathrm{U}\), and \(+7\) in \(\mathrm{Np}\).

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Chromate–dichromate equilibrium depends on \(\mathrm{pH}\), permanganate requires a non-reducing acid for titrations, lanthanoid contraction equalises \(4d\) and \(5d\) radii, and early actinoids utilise \(5f\), \(6d\), and \(7s\) electrons to achieve high oxidation states.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Claim
The claim regarding chromate and dichromate is correct: adding acid converts yellow \(\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}\) to orange \(\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}\) and adding base reverses the process, with \(\mathrm{Cr}\) remaining in the \(+6\) state. The claim regarding hydrochloric acid in permanganate titrations is incorrect: \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) oxidises \(\mathrm{HCl}\) to \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\), making \(\mathrm{HCl}\) unsuitable. The claim regarding \(\mathrm{Zr}\) and \(\mathrm{Hf}\) is correct: lanthanoid contraction due to poor shielding by \(4f\) electrons makes their radii nearly identical. The claim regarding early actinoid oxidation states is correct: maximum oxidation states rise from \(+4\) (\(\mathrm{Th}\)) to \(+5\) (\(\mathrm{Pa}\)), \(+6\) (\(\mathrm{U}\)), and \(+7\) (\(\mathrm{Np}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Only the claims regarding chromate–dichromate interconversion, lanthanoid contraction in \(\mathrm{Zr}/\mathrm{Hf}\), and early actinoid maximum oxidation states are correct.
